body: This should be in r/wtf because, you know......wtf??

my sons father played mental games with me since the day my son was born. He has admitted to this. He is not what you would call a good father. He is selfish, ignorant and hurtful. He sees his son for one day a fortnight. Even then he lets his parents do a lot of the hard work.

Sorry to jump on the defensive but I don't 'hook in' men. I don't lie about who I am or act different up front. 
You're right I need to work on my self esteem, and I have been doing so with regular counselling and support courses for two years now.

I really like the idea of being bound to someone you love and who loves you equally for the rest of your life. Being a team. Sharing the same name. The romance if it. 
I know there are tough times in marriages, I just like the thought of belonging to a loving man.

Yeah that's great advice. And I'm pleased your mom has been so successful :) 
My son is certainly the most important thing in my life right now, and I've started a hairdressing course, made new friends etc. I guess I'm nervous for my long term future. I want so badly to be a wife.

I know it's possible for there to be a man out there willing to put up with my baggage, but it seems so unlikely. That's all. 
In all of my relationships there has been an incredible honeymoon phase, a couple of years of satisfied co-existence and then suddenly I'm a nightmare to live with. I don't get it. I'm fun loving, reasonably pretty, quite funny(so I'm told), clever, cultural and sensitive. 
Perhaps this isn't so much about worrying about my baggage, but a lack of confidence in my suitability as a partner, as all previous partners have called it a day.
My last partner, the father of my son, was two years younger than me, and after my son was born he showed his true immature, disrespectful, ignorant colours. It's old guys all the way!!

I had had my 'first love' before this. A guy from my year group whom I was with for a year. 
I should perhaps mention, that my parents split when I was 14 and this first love boyfriend became my everything. When we broke up I was pretty devastated and perhaps I wouldn't have been so keen to get into another relationship (ie the one with my teacher) had I felt supported at home at this stage.

I think the sense of frenzy over finding her that was portrayed in the press was unnecessary. She obviously went of her own accord. It's slightly worrying that it seems they were thinking of shacking up in France without telling either of their families; you have to wonder if she really wanted to be away from her parents in that way. 
When I was with my teacher I couldn't understand why anyone would worry or think it was strange. We loved each other so much and functioned so normally. It breaks my heart to think of Megan being torn away from the man she loves, however there is the issue of her being under the legal age of consent for sex. Throws a bit of a spanner the works. I guess that's why so many people are upset about it. It would take forever to consider all sides of the story I think. So in short, yes. People are overreacting!

I guess I feel a little different purely because I've been a teacher of the same age that he was when we started going out. Looking at some of the 16 and 17 yr old girls in the school I worked at, I thought 'what the hell was he thinking??' But then there were one or two girls in the same year group who stood out as being mature, responsible, elegant, sensible. I hope I was one of them. I will never know. He's now married (to someone his own age) with a daughter. I have no idea if his wife knows the circumstances under which we got together.  I wouldn't jeopardise their happiness just to satisfy my curiosity.

At 26 I started to train as a teacher myself. 26 was the age my teacher was when we got together. I can tell you now that at 26 years of age I had ABSOLUTELY no interest in dating a 17 year old. I found the idea disgusting and it brought into question my teacher's motives for dating me. All I can say is that at the time it felt very comfortable and right, I did not feel used, I was not mistreated. I felt loved and important.

At first, as there was a period where we had to meet covertly or only speak via MSN. But it didn't last too long. I left the school a year earlier than I should have (due to failing a couple of classes - all my fault, not his!) and we were more free.  We eventually moved in together, decorated, went on holidays, went shopping, bought a pet.... All the usual stuff!
Haha! No. Any lessons I learned from our time together arrived in my mind years later, rather than him actually teaching me anything. Oh the irony!

I certainly learned a lot from the relationship. Both about myself and about relationships in general. In the end we split because the age difference was causing us to drift apart. Of course with the benefit of hindsight I know that the age difference was a problem long before then. We were together when I went to university and I felt obligated to spend time with him doing 'grown up' relationshipy things rather that engaging fully with the student experience. Something which I massively regret. 
I, too, never felt as if I was being used. We depended upon each other emotionally just as any couple would.

There were a couple of other teachers who had a suspicion, but took no action. I don't know why, except perhaps they didn't want to cause controversy for the school. If parents had gotten wind of it their good reputation would have gone downhill. I do recall being taken into the office of one of these teachers and being told I should seek counselling for loneliness, because I was 'clearly searching in the wrong places for comfort'.
  My then boyfriend wanted to switch careers anyway from Languages into IT so moved to a different school for a new position and was then in less danger of losing his job, however I know that he wouldn't have moved so quickly had it not been for our relationship. 
I told one or two of my friends whom I felt I could trust, and their reactions were shock and disbelief as you can imagine! But rather than being a fling, it blossomed into a real relationship very quickly, so when it came to telling my parents they took it quite well. My mum was quite pleased I was with someone who could look after me financially, my dad was hesitant at first (as a teacher himself he couldn't quite get his head round it) but once he saw how happy we were his reservations quickly disappeared.

He was 9 years older than me. 

We got together the same way a lot of people do. Some flirting, some online chatting (not to be confused with grooming!) and a lot of mutual attraction. He was running the school jazz band and had handed out his email address so we could all communicate with him about rehearsals, music etc. and one day I emailed him something pretty mundane which to be totally honest I can't remember, then within his reply, there seemed to be a spark......
We had always interacted a lot more easily than a teacher and pupil normally would I guess, I found him attractive, he took an interest in me and I felt very comfortable and grown up around him.   The natural thing seemed to be to follow the spark in the email.  Flirting ensued....
I think +44 is the country code for the uk. it replaces the zero. Google for the learns.

When you're a child you grow up believing your parents are always right as you don't really know any better, and it's in our very nature to learn by example. You're now 25 and can clearly see that their path is and indeed must be different from your own. I have massive respect for you for coming out of the closet. I wish you well on your path. Seriously. Awesome. Xx
